_comment: Mutation-coverage floors per crate, compared by .github/scripts/mutants-gate.py. The floor ratchets: a run may hold or improve it and may not fall below it. `target_caught_pct` is what docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md requires for release sign-off, and it is the destination rather than the floor — a gate that failed from day one would be switched off in a week. Record a new floor with `mise run mutants-baseline --expect-shards sunrise-sync=1` locally, naming the crates and shard counts the run actually covered, or `mutants-gate.py <outcomes...> --update --expect-shards sunrise-domain=6,sunrise-core=4,sunrise-crypto=2,sunrise-sync=1` from a nightly's artifacts, in a commit that says what was added to earn it. The shard counts are not optional: `--update` banks whatever it is handed, so without them one shard of a crate becomes that crate's floor. Pass `--allow-partial` instead only when a floor covering just what ran is what you actually want. Every crate the run scores must appear here: the gate fails on a crate it measured and has no floor for, because a crate scored against nothing is a crate it is not protecting. `sunrise-core` is deliberately absent rather than seeded with a placeholder — a full pass over it is hours, so its floor is recorded from the first run that completes one, and until then the gate says so out loud. That rule named `sunrise-domain` too, and said both floors "are recorded from the first nightly run's artifacts". A complete local pass supersedes it, and this file now records `sunrise-domain`'s floor from one. The supersession is deliberate and the reason is the placeholder, not the nightly: the rule exists to stop a crate whose full pass is hours being seeded with a number nobody measured, and a complete 1356-mutant pass is not a placeholder wherever it ran. What it does not supersede is the `sunrise-core` half — that crate has no complete pass, local or nightly, so it stays absent, and #246 holds it. Provenance of the re-recorded floors, because a floor that cannot be compared with the one it replaced is a number without a claim. `sunrise-crypto`'s and `sunrise-sync`'s were first measured on 2026-09-16, locally and single-shard — but not at the same revision, and not by one invocation; `sunrise-sync`'s has since been superseded, and the paragraph at the end of this comment is that measurement. `sunrise-crypto` was measured at 1d4b484 and recorded by `mise run mutants-baseline --expect-shards sunrise-crypto=1`. `sunrise-sync` was measured at 164cc76, the commit that adds the three tests, and recorded by `mise run mutants-baseline --expect-shards sunrise-sync=1`; 1d4b484 predates those tests and measures 36.89% on the same population, so recording sunrise-sync against it would name a revision that does not produce that number. That floor stood at 59/122 = 48.36% until the pass recorded at the end of this comment replaced it. One invocation per crate is what keeps each floor's revision its own: the task globs every outcomes file under out/mutants/ and hands the lot to the gate, and `--update` merges into this file per crate rather than replacing it, so the crates named in `--expect-shards` must be the crates whose results are on disk — a crate with outcomes and no expectation is a configuration error the gate refuses. Neither is a like-for-like improvement on its predecessor. `sunrise-crypto` went 78.43% -> 85.47% over a population that grew 296 -> 519 mutants as the crate did, and #96's six device-certificate width mutants -- the four field-width match guards and both `nickname.len() > 64` checks -- are confirmed caught in this run. `sunrise-sync` went 27.17% -> 48.36%, and most of that is not a test improvement at all: the old figure was measured without `--all-features`, which left all 94 of `src/sse.rs`'s mutants compiled out and therefore scored missed, so it described a build configuration. Same tree, feature on, before any test was added: 36.89%. See #193 and docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md §Features. The remaining 11.5 points are three tests added with it. `sunrise-sync`'s one timeout (`TokenSource::set` replaced with `()`) sits in the denominator and not the numerator, which is why that rate was 59/122 = 48.36% and not the 60/122 that scoring it as caught would give. 48.76% is 59/121, which is dropping the timeout from the denominator altogether — how the gate treats `unviable`, not how it would treat a caught mutant. `sunrise-domain`'s counterfactual below is computed by the caught rule, and that one matched it. `sunrise-domain`'s floor is that first full pass, run locally at 1d4b484 on 2026-09-16 and recorded by its own `mise run mutants-baseline --expect-shards sunrise-domain=1`: 1356 mutants in 2h, single shard, nothing extrapolated. The counts reconcile against what the rest of the repository records independently: 1004 + 197 + 23 + 132 = 1356, the population .github/workflows/ci.yml's matrix comment and docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md's cost table each carry on their own, and 1004 / (1356 - 132 unviable) = 1004/1224 = 82.03% by the gate's own rule. Its 23 timeouts are worth knowing before anyone reads the 82.03% as brittle. Every one of them is `+=` replaced with `-=` or `*=` on a cursor advance in a `parse` loop — 14 in capture.rs, 6 in sort_order.rs, 3 in annotate.rs — so they are non-terminating mutants rather than a slow machine, and they will be 23 on any machine. They sit in the denominator and not the numerator: counting them as caught would read 83.90% and would mean an infinite loop had improved the score. What they do say is that those parse loops have no asserted progress guarantee, which is a real gap and a separate piece of work from recording this floor: it is filed as #245, and #245 is where moving this floor belongs. Recording the floor at all is not free, and the cost sits here beside it. The gate ratchets, so 82.03% is a standing constraint from now on — on a crate neither #96 nor #193 asked to constrain, enforced against six CI shards from a measurement taken on one. What bounds that is `.cargo/mutants.toml`'s `timeout_multiplier = 5.0` and `minimum_test_timeout = 120`, both relative to a per-invocation baseline, so a slower runner gets a proportionally longer mutant timeout rather than a spurious breach. `sunrise-sync`'s floor was re-recorded on 2026-09-19 at `a44001c`, by `mutants-gate.py out/mutants/sunrise-sync/mutants.out/outcomes.json --update --expect-shards sunrise-sync=1`, one local single-shard pass of 136 mutants in 7m: 60 caught, 61 missed, 1 timeout, 14 unviable, 60/122 = 49.18%. The revision is `a44001c` and not this branch's tip because `a44001c` is the last commit that changes code — the tip changes only this file — and every other floor above names its own for the reason this paragraph would otherwise drop: a floor whose revision is not named cannot be compared with the one it replaced. It replaces 59/122 = 48.36%, measured at `164cc76`, and #244 called the move in advance, because that change removes `TokenWatch::seen` together with the test that killed its mutants. What earned the number back, and then some, is the same change rewriting `TokenWatch::mark_current` to return `Option<u64>` from `Ref::has_changed()` and asserting both of its arms: the population moved 135 -> 136 as the two effects netted out, and the rate moved up 0.82 points rather than down the 0.86 that removing two caught mutants alone would have cost. That population move supersedes the three `sunrise-sync` 135s recorded elsewhere, and supersedes them only from `a44001c` forward: `.cargo/mutants.toml:104`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:633` and `docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md:295` each name `1d4b484` explicitly and remain correct at the revision they name, while `docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md:247`'s cost table names no revision for its mutant column and is the one of the four a reader can take as current. None of the three is a floor, so none is load-bearing for the gate, and repointing them is not this file's business — but a reader meeting 135 and 136 should know the difference is the crate moving and not drift. One sentence that stood here has been withdrawn rather than repeated: that the single timeout is the same `TokenSource::set` mutant as before and is scored the same way. It is probably true and it is not verifiable from this repository — `out/` is neither committed nor produced by any pull-request check, so the outcomes file that would name the mutant is not here to read. What "like for like" actually rests on is that both rates are computed by the same rule, which is checkable and holds.
